predictions.prediction_note: The lead proposed aliases >= 3/5. I register 4/5 and state why: the D1 CPU check (artifacts/grm_d1/alias_cpu_aplus.json) shows the fold firing, the digest naming BOTH names, being ADMITTED and MOUNTED, and serving the right value for 10/10 alias probes at every distance, with a 78-token digest inside the 96 width. The one reservation that keeps me off 5/5 is that the CPU reader is a regex double: the GPU reader must still choose the digest value over the surrounding prose, and LT1 already showed one long-distance ladder drop (recall_3_150) that no lineage change addresses. 4/5 prices exactly one such drop.

finding.detail: H1 measured correctly: on-tree graft_arena.py != the amendment-1 pin. Measured by this seat, both arms: lt1_1_preflight -> BLOCKED, reasons = [INPUT_SHA_MISMATCH: core/graft_arena.py, INPUT_SHA_MISMATCH: core/graft_repository.py, INPUT_SHA_MISMATCH: core/grm_alias_fold.py]. The order named two FIX-9 files and alias_fold; the third blocked pin (core/graft_repository.py) is also FIX-9, so the blocked set is three files, not two.
finding.marks_were_hiding_the_blocker: THE MARKS DID NOT MERELY LABEL THE BLOCKER -- THEY SUPPRESSED IT. tests/conftest.py:75-124 makes `campaign_receipt` a SKIP-BY-DEFAULT marker. With the marks in place the two files reported "25 passed, 12 skipped" on a tree whose preflight was BLOCKED: skip-green, not green. Removing the marks is what makes the gate able to fail; the rebind is what makes it pass.

defects_the_unmarking_exposed.env_leak: Every test taking the `pinned` fixture failed GRM_ENV_LEAK. The guard (tests/conftest.py:198-226) runs at the END OF THE CALL PHASE by design, but a yield-fixture cleans up at TEARDOWN, so `pinned_arm`'s correct finally-restore was too late to be seen. Fixed by registering the same keys with `monkeypatch` in the fixture, which the guard recognises as pinned. `pinned_arm` still does the real pin and its readback.
defects_the_unmarking_exposed.note: Removing the marks made these tests run for the first time on this tree. Both defects are in OUR test file and predate amendment 8; the marks had been hiding them.
defects_the_unmarking_exposed.teeth_pointed_at_a_superseded_block: The two planted-drift teeth tests planted into amendment 1. Once amendment 8 governs, that block is never consulted, so the tests proved nothing and failed with AMENDMENT2_CHAIN_MISMATCH. Fixed with `_governing()` (plant in the block the runner actually reads) and `_replant()` (repair the downstream previous_amendment_sha256 links so the planted drift is the ONLY defect, and the INPUT check is what fails). The teeth are now sharper than before: they follow the governing block instead of a hard-coded amendment number.

marks_removed.note: 8 marks in the preflight file and 1 in the amendment3 file, per the lead. These tests are ours and now run by default.

fix.runner_reads_the_governing_rebind: scripts/grm_lt1_1.py previously read `core_rebind` from AMENDMENT1 at four sites, so no later amendment could rebind a pin. Added `governing_core_rebind()` / `governing_core_pins()`: the newest amendment carrying a `core_rebind` governs, which is the rule the preflight already applied to the runner binding. Byte-identical behaviour on a tree where nothing moved.

follow_up_instruction: Amendment 8 rebinds pins only. It makes NO measurement claim: the CPU numbers in amendment 7 were taken on the pre-merge core and are NOT restated here as results for this tree.

prior_art.fix9_and_a1a3: Not this seat's work - SCOUT-FIX-9 and A1 amendment 3 are the lead-merged core changes this amendment binds to. Their own prior-art annotations live at their code sites; core/grm_alias_fold.py:213-216 credits SC1.1/FIX-8 for the glyph-shattering class.
prior_art.governing_rebind: No prior art known to me for this specific rule; it is the ordinary "latest record wins" of an append-only amendment chain (append-only timestamped ledgers, Haber & Stornetta 1991, in kind). The "LATEST amendment governs" phrasing is this campaign's own, from the runner-binding logic already in lt1_1_preflight. Unverified against literature - no network in this sandbox; lead to check. Search terms: "append-only amendment chain", "latest-wins record supersession", "content-addressed pin rebinding".

purpose: Rebind LT1.1 core input pins to the merged tree it must run on. LT1.1 measures the core that ships; after the grm-merge fast-forward brought SCOUT-FIX-9 and A1 amendment 3 into core/, the amendment-1 pins were superseded and the chain preflight was BLOCKED with INPUT_SHA_MISMATCH on three files.
ruling: LT1's original registration is a frozen receipt of its day; it is NOT re-validated against today's core. LT1.1's host preflight must validate LT1.1's own chain — registration 02b44d02 + amendments 1–3, whose core pins were rebound to this tree with attribution — using the same verification functions (`grm_lt1.verify`-class checks: sha-bound inputs, fixture sha, cell schedule, budget) but pointed at LT1.1's registration/amendment set. LT1's registration sha and its recorded core pins are carried as `parent` lineage in the LT1.1 receipt (recorded, with the drift table you already attributed), not as a gate.
